findings.description: If the failure happens after os.replace (or the temp file is already gone), os.unlink(tmp_name) raises FileNotFoundError inside the except block. That exception replaces the real write error and `raise` is never reached. The bare `except:` also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.
findings.suggestion: Use `except BaseException:` with `contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError)` around the unlink, or `except Exception:`, then re-raise the original error.
findings.title: Bare except with unguarded unlink can mask the original error

findings.description: super()._commit(sessions) runs after os.replace has already published the file. The in-memory assignment is trivial and unlikely to fail. But the unlink handler covers only the file operations, so any failure between the replace and the memory swap leaves disk and memory out of sync.
findings.suggestion: Keep the memory swap immediately adjacent to the replace and ensure no failure can occur between them.
findings.title: Memory update after replace can diverge from disk
